message: My phone rang while I was eating lunch at a local restaurant.  "I have a collect call for [static] from [static] will you accept?"  Before I can say anything, the phone seems to go dead.  Then someone else is speaking and the only thing I could understand for "Queene Ane County Prison".  Well, it turns out that my granddaughter's father is in that institution , I think.  The voice changes again and a man explains that if I want to speak to the caller I have to set up an account.  It sounded very strange to me.  He said I would need to give him some information so that he could set up my account, and he started asking me questions, name, address, last four digits of my Social Security Number.  He asked me to spell every word no matter how simple the word was.  He then explains that the best way to set up this account is to use a credit card.  Ding, ding, ding!!  The bells and whistles start ringing.  There is no way on earth that I am gong to give anyone my credit card number especially since I still do not even know at that point who he is and what organization he represents.  He tells me that the least I can give him is $50 plus an $8 fee, and the maximum is $500 with the same $8 fee.  I ask him who it was that wanted to talk to me, to which he replied that he was not permitted to give out that information.  The whole thing has got to be a scam, I think, so I ask for the company's snail mail address, and he surprized me by giving me one.  I told him I would call him back later today or send the money to him via snail mail.  He sort of"sneared" at that when he said that it takes at least ten day to set up the through the mail.  I said "thanks" and hung up the phone.  I googled T-Netix and wow! a bonanza of information every single bit of it quite negative!  How much danger am I in for having given him the last four digits of my SSN?  Is there something I can do to prevent him found using it to steal my identity?  Obviously the state's are not interested in helping us.
